person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: what constitutes a type of neurone, and which partial measures are sufficient to recognise one within an area, across areas and across species
span.quote: Of course, in most cases only some of the measures will be available in a given experiment, and one of the important current tasks is to establish which partial measures are sufficient for the correct recognition of a class of cell, in one cortical area, across areas and across different species.

span.label: whether interneurone classes defined by their input and output synapses and their molecular expression also occupy distinct positions in time, firing at characteristic phases of network oscillations
span.quote: Here we attempt to define cell types first on the distribution of input and output synapses coupled with protein expression, then show that at least some cell types defined this way exhibit distinct firing patterns in vivo , placing each interneurone type to a distinct position in a multidimensional space of spatial, molecular and temporal measures.

span.label: at least 16 GABAergic types are enumerated against explicit criteria, and four of them are shown to fire at type-specific phases that change between brain states
span.quote: Reviewing the cell types and their spatio-temporal interactions, we suggest that CA1 pyramidal cells are supported by at least 16 distinct types of GABAergic neurone. During a given behaviour-contingent network oscillation, interneurones of a given type exhibit similar firing patterns.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: These results suggest roles for specific interneurone types in structuring the activity of pyramidal cells via their respective target domains, and accurately timing and synchronizing pyramidal cell discharge, rather than providing generalized inhibition.

span.label: cell-type-specific interneurone firing during hippocampal network oscillations
span.quote: During a given behaviour-contingent network oscillation, interneurones of a given type exhibit similar firing patterns.

span.label: review
span.quote: In the present review we focus on the CA1 area of the rat hippocampus, as potentially the simplest area of the cerebral cortex with particularly well-characterized oscillatory activity patterns ( Vanderwolf, 1969 ), in order to dissect the potential contribution of different cell types to distinct network states.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Because each interneurone class terminates on a different pyramidal-cell compartment and each class fires at a different phase, the compartments of one pyramidal cell receive GABAergic input separated in time, which structures where and when that cell can integrate its inputs.
span.quote: Because the different interneurones innervate distinct domains of the pyramidal cells, the different compartments will receive differential GABAergic input in time.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: During ripples the interneurones act not by shunting spikes but by delivering hyperpolarization timed to de-inactivate voltage-dependent ion channels, which then promotes the pyramidal cells' next discharge.
span.quote: This specific spike timing indicates that the role for the interneurones during ripple episodes lies not in the shunting of action potentials, but, more likely, in providing hyperpolarization well-timed to de-inactivate voltage-dependent ion channels and therefore promote subsequent firing of pyramidal cells.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: O-LM cells go silent during ripples partly because their pyramidal input has a very low resting release probability that only repetitive presynaptic firing raises, and pyramidal cells emit only one or two spikes per ripple.
span.quote: The pyramidal input to O-LM cells has a very low resting release probability, which is increased only by repetitive firing ( Ali et al. 1999 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Bistratified cells firing at ripple frequency before the pyramidal cells could structure dendritic oscillations so that accumulating excitation triggers fast dendritic spikes that propagate to the soma.
span.quote: In particular, the early ripple frequency firing of bistratified cells, before the pyramidal cells, could structure dendritic oscillations in the pyramidal cell dendrites and with the build-up of excitation lead to fast dendritic spikes actively propagating to the soma

span.label: different interneurone types innervate different domains of the pyramidal cell, so the compartments receive GABAergic input differentiated in time rather than generalized inhibition
span.quote: And finally, interneurones belonging to different connectivity classes may fire preferentially at distinct time points during a given oscillation. Because the different interneurones innervate distinct domains of the pyramidal cells, the different compartments will receive differential GABAergic input in time. Such a dynamic spatio-temporal GABAergic control, which evolves distinct patterns during different brain states, is ideally suited to regulating the input integration of individual pyramidal cells and contribute to the formation of cell assemblies and representations in the hippocampus.

span.label: perisomatic cells fire before the pyramidal cells and can reset intrinsic membrane oscillations, which is how a single cell can synchronise thousands
span.quote: If a single basket cell innervating up to 2000 pyramidal cells ( Sik et al. 1995 ; Halasy et al. 1996 ) can reset the rhythmic firing of the cells and synchronize them in interaction with intrinsic membrane oscillations, how would the approximately 25 basket cells converging on a single pyramidal cell ( Buhl et al. 1994 a ) affect firing in different brain states?

span.label: and the same class fires differently in different brain states, so its target domain is modulated in a brain-state-dependent way
span.quote: These results indicate that interneurones within a connectivity class (nos (1), (2), (5) and (6) reported so far) exhibit similar firing patterns during a given network oscillation. In addition, during different network oscillations representing two distinct brain states, interneurones of the same connectivity class show different firing activities and therefore modulate their specific postsynaptic target-domain in a brain-state-dependent manner.

span.label: with the silence of one class during ripples not explicable by weak excitation alone, so an additional silencing mechanism must exist in the network
span.quote: The silence of O-LM cells during ripple episodes is surprising because they receive their major glutamatergic input from local CA1 pyramidal cells, which are most active as a population during ripples. The pyramidal input to O-LM cells has a very low resting release probability, which is increased only by repetitive firing ( Ali et al. 1999 ). Because pyramidal cells rarely fire more than one or two action potentials, this network state is not optimal for O-LM cell activation. However, the specific depression of firing of O-LM cells during ripple episodes cannot be explained by weak excitation alone. Additional mechanisms for silencing must be present in the network.

span.label: Controversial data and divergent views are not treated critically, for reasons of length.
span.note: what this limits: the review's treatment of disputed evidence: DUE TO SPACE LIMITATION WE CANNOT DEAL CRITICALLY WITH ALL THE CONTROVERSIAL DATA OR DIVERGENT VIEWS
span.quote: Due to space limitation we cannot deal critically with all the controversial data or divergent views (see Parra et al. 1998 ).

span.label: Several of the listed classes rest on very little evidence, sometimes from a single laboratory.
span.note: what this limits: the evidential weight behind individual classes: ON SOME CELLS VERY LITTLE INFORMATION EXISTS AND SOMETIMES EVEN THAT ONLY FROM ONE LABORATORY
span.quote: We would like to emphasize that on some cells very little information exists and sometimes even that only from one laboratory; but revealing how little we know may facilitate more detailed tests.

span.label: The central firing-pattern claim rests on in vivo data from only four of the many interneurone classes.
span.note: what this limits: the firing-pattern claim specifically: THE IN VIVO FIRING PATTERNS OF ONLY FOUR DISTINCT CLASSES OF INTERNEURONE HAVE BEEN REPORTED, ALTHOUGH MANY MORE TYPES EXIST
span.quote: So far, the in vivo firing patterns of only four distinct classes of interneurone have been reported, although many more types of interneurone exist.

span.label: The proposed list of cell types is explicitly provisional.
span.note: what this limits: the list of cell types itself: ONGOING STUDIES WILL MODIFY THIS LIST, though the number of distinct GABA sources is unlikely to shrink
span.quote: Undoubtedly, ongoing studies will modify this list, but the number of distinct sources of GABA is unlikely to become smaller.

span.label: on some cells very little information exists and sometimes even that only from one laboratory, but revealing how little we know may facilitate more detailed tests
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1 - single-laboratory evidence behind some classes
span.quote: We would like to emphasize that on some cells very little information exists and sometimes even that only from one laboratory; but revealing how little we know may facilitate more detailed tests.

span.label: and names which of its own entries may be lumped together once more is known - the back-projection and hippocampo-septal cells, the two perforant path classes, and some of the three interneurone-specific ones
span.note: what this limits: the boundaries between the listed classes: SOME OF THE ABOVE LISTED CELL CLASSES MAY BE LUMPED OR SPLIT FURTHER WHEN SUFFICIENT INFORMATION BECOMES AVAILABLE ON ALL ASPECTS THAT DEFINE A CELL CLASS WITH OUR CRITERIA
span.quote: Some of the above listed cell classes may be lumped or split further when sufficient information becomes available on all aspects that define a cell class with our criteria. In particular, the backprojection and septo-hippocampal cells (nos (12) and (13)), the two classes of perforant path-associated cells (nos (8) and (9)) and some of the three classes of interneurone specific cells (nos (14)–(16)) may prove to be members of a single population.

span.label: two of the listed types differ only in which of two molecules they express, and may be two states of one cell type rather than two types
span.note: what this limits: the distinctness of two specific types: IT CANNOT BE EXCLUDED THAT THE EXPRESSION OF VIP AND VGLUT3 IS DYNAMICALLY REGULATED IN TIME - they may be one cell in two states, not two types
span.quote: As in further cases below, when so little information is available, it cannot be excluded that the expression of VIP and VGLUT3 is dynamically regulated in time and that types (3) and (4) are two states of one cell type. Further data on synaptic connectivity, additional molecular constituents known to occur in cortical CCK + interneurones such as CRF, preprotachikinin B, 5-HT3 receptor, etc., intrinsic membrane properties and in vivo firing patterns are needed to test this possibility.

span.label: no molecular marker separates the axo-axonic cell from the parvalbumin basket cell, so electron microscopy is needed to tell them apart
span.note: what this limits: the axo-axonic versus basket-cell distinction: NO MOLECULAR MARKER HAS BEEN REPORTED TO SEPARAT[E them], so the distinction requires electron microscopy
span.quote: The expression of parvalbumin in the soma, dendrites and terminals ( Katsumaru et al. 1988 ) is common with some of the basket cells; no molecular marker has been reported to separate axo-axonic and PV + basket cells.

span.label: and the coexistence patterns of the markers leave a large unexplained heterogeneity that may hide further classes
span.note: what this limits: the completeness of the classification: THE COEXISTENCE PATTERNS OF MOLECULAR CELL MARKERS PREDICT SOME CLEAR SEPARATIONS, BUT ALSO A LARGE AS YET UNEXPLAINED HETEROGENEITY, INDICATING POSSIBLE FURTHER DISTINCT CELL CLASSES
span.quote: The coexistence patterns of molecular cell markers predict some clear separations, but also a large as yet unexplained heterogeneity, indicating possible further distinct cell classes. For example, 5-HT3 receptor, CCK and CB1 receptor expression strongly overlaps ( Morales & Bloom, 1997 , Morales et al. 2004 ; Katona et al. 1999 b ; Tsou et al. 1999 ), but it is not yet clear whether all CCK expressing cells express the receptors or only some of the cell types (nos (3), (4) and (7)–(9)) defined above. Only mapping these molecules to cells with full axonal and dendritic arborizations and revealing their firing patterns can lead to clear cell identification.

span.label: Ramon y Cajal's and Lorente de No's cell descriptions, most of which were then ignored or collapsed into one name
span.quote: Although the identity of the basket cell has not been questioned, the many other cell types described by Ramon y Cajal (1893) and Lorente de No (1934) have either been ignored and all non-pyramidal cells called basket cells, or non-pyramidal cells were named by the laminar location of their soma, or some other simple feature, as if that would define a cell type as outlined above.

span.label: molecular markers as class criteria - adopted, and then shown to be insufficient on their own
span.quote: With the cited evidence we hope to convince our readers that some frequently used criteria about the identity of interneurones are unsustainable. (i) Somatic location in a layer does not identify an interneurone class, as the same class may have somata in several layers and all layers contain several distinct classes. (ii) Dendritic shape does not necessarily identify an interneurone class, as indistinguishable axonal output can be made by cells having diverse dendritic fields. (iii) A single molecular cell marker, such as a calcium binding protein or a neuropeptide, does not identify an interneurone class on its own, as most molecules have been shown to be expressed in several different cell types with distinct inputs and spatio-temporal outputs. For example, parvalbumin is expressed by at least four distinct classes of interneurone (see below).

span.label: the homologous cell classes, and the axo-axonic cell which was discovered there first
span.quote: Most of the GABAergic cell types defined in the CA1 area have homologues in the isocortex, which is particularly apparent in the supragranular layers. For example, the somata of supragranular pyramidal cells are innervated by basket cells immunopositive for PV, or CCK, or CCK and VGLUT3 ( Kawaguchi & Kubota, 1997 ; Somogyi et al. 2004 ) as in the hippocampus, and the axo-axonic cell was discovered in the rat visual cortex.

span.label: oscillation-phase firing, imported as the fourth axis of the definition rather than as a result
span.quote: Probably all neurones of the cortex can be defined, recognized and compared on the comprehensive application of the following measures: (i) brain area- and cell domain-specific distribution of input and output synapses, (ii) expression of proteins involved in cell signalling, (iii) intrinsic membrane properties reflecting the expression of ion channel proteins, and (iv) temporal distribution of firing in vivo . Based on the above range of parameters, each cell will fall into a tight cluster, the cell type , in this multidimensional space.

span.label: cell type
span.quote: Based on the above range of parameters, each cell will fall into a tight cluster, the cell type , in this multidimensional space.

span.label: marker
span.quote: Note that one molecular cell marker may be expressed by several distinct cell types.

span.label: heterogeneity
span.quote: The coexistence patterns of molecular cell markers predict some clear separations, but also a large as yet unexplained heterogeneity

span.label: basket cell
span.quote: The basket cell then was the first inhibitory neurone identified in the brain 70 years later.

span.label: parvalbumin
span.quote: For example, parvalbumin is expressed by at least four distinct classes of interneurone

span.label: axo-axonic cells → parvalbumin positive basket cells
span.note: THE TWO CANNOT BE SEPARATED IN THIS STUDY - the DESIGN form of the negative relation (Q-286/Q-287). No edge type can express it: all eight assert that a relation HOLDS. A confounding statement bounds what the paper's own results can mean, and it lives where nothing downstream will find it. SCOPED TO A METHOD, which makes it the second case after marill1956 where the negative relation carries its own respect: 'WITHOUT ELECTRON MICROSCOPIC EXAMINATION, in some cases, the cells cannot be distinguished'. The distinction is drawable - with the right instrument. This is the paper whose subject is that cell types are defined by the features tested, saying it about its own two types.
span.quote: In most but not all cases, axo-axonic cells can be recognized from the shape of the axon terminal segments; therefore, without electron microscopic examination, in some cases, the cells cannot be distinguished from parvalbumin positive basket cells.

span.label: interneurones → domains
span.note: THE RELATION THE SPAN ACTUALLY ASSERTS: different interneurones innervate DISTINCT DOMAINS of the pyramidal cells, so the different compartments receive differential GABAergic input IN TIME. The anatomy is the cause and the timing is what the oscillation contributes - two separate things the retracted edge collapsed into one.
span.quote: And finally, interneurones belonging to different connectivity classes may fire preferentially at distinct time points during a given oscillation. Because the different interneurones innervate distinct domains of the pyramidal cells, the different compartments will receive differential GABAergic input in time. Such a dynamic spatio-temporal GABAergic control, which evolves distinct patterns during different brain states, is ideally suited to regulating the input integration of individual pyramidal cells and contribute to the formation of cell assemblies and representations in the hippocampus.

span.label: THIS PROJECT'S OWN PROBLEM, STATED IN 2005 ABOUT NEURONES: there is no agreement on the criteria of what is necessary to define a type, and consequently different authors use PARTIAL CRITERIA OR SETS OF NON-OVERLAPPING DATA for studying the same or a mixture of several populations
span.quote: There is no agreement on the number and identity of neuronal species in the cerebral cortex. This is partly due to the lack of agreement on criteria of what is necessary to define a cell type, and consequently different authors use partial criteria or sets of non-overlapping data for studying the same or a mixture of several neuronal populations.

span.label: AND THE TASK IS NAMED EXACTLY AS THIS PROJECT WOULD NAME IT: to establish WHICH PARTIAL MEASURES ARE SUFFICIENT for the correct recognition of a class, in one area, across areas, and across species
span.quote: Of course, in most cases only some of the measures will be available in a given experiment, and one of the important current tasks is to establish which partial measures are sufficient for the correct recognition of a class of cell, in one cortical area, across areas and across different species.

span.label: a definition given as a position in a multidimensional space: four measures applied together, with each cell falling into a tight cluster which IS the cell type
span.quote: Probably all neurones of the cortex can be defined, recognized and compared on the comprehensive application of the following measures: (i) brain area- and cell domain-specific distribution of input and output synapses, (ii) expression of proteins involved in cell signalling, (iii) intrinsic membrane properties reflecting the expression of ion channel proteins, and (iv) temporal distribution of firing in vivo . Based on the above range of parameters, each cell will fall into a tight cluster, the cell type , in this multidimensional space.

span.label: THREE CRITERIA THAT DO NOT WORK, LISTED AS SUCH: somatic location in a layer, dendritic shape, and a single molecular marker - since parvalbumin alone is expressed by at least four distinct classes
span.quote: With the cited evidence we hope to convince our readers that some frequently used criteria about the identity of interneurones are unsustainable. (i) Somatic location in a layer does not identify an interneurone class, as the same class may have somata in several layers and all layers contain several distinct classes. (ii) Dendritic shape does not necessarily identify an interneurone class, as indistinguishable axonal output can be made by cells having diverse dendritic fields. (iii) A single molecular cell marker, such as a calcium binding protein or a neuropeptide, does not identify an interneurone class on its own, as most molecules have been shown to be expressed in several different cell types with distinct inputs and spatio-temporal outputs. For example, parvalbumin is expressed by at least four distinct classes of interneurone (see below).

span.label: AND A NAME APPLIED TOO WIDELY DESTROYS THE DISTINCTIONS: the other types Ramon y Cajal described were ignored and all non-pyramidal cells called basket cells, or named by the layer of their soma, AS IF THAT WOULD DEFINE A CELL TYPE
span.quote: Although the identity of the basket cell has not been questioned, the many other cell types described by Ramon y Cajal (1893) and Lorente de No (1934) have either been ignored and all non-pyramidal cells called basket cells, or non-pyramidal cells were named by the laminar location of their soma, or some other simple feature, as if that would define a cell type as outlined above.

span.label: with the correction arriving a century later - even basket cells, defined by where they terminate, belong to several distinct classes, and the laminar location of a soma does not define anything
span.quote: A rigorous analysis of individual cells with several methods has shown that even basket cells, as defined by terminating on pyramidal somata, belong to several distinct classes (see below), and the laminar location of an interneurone soma does not define it.

span.label: ONE NAME OVER SEVERAL REFERENTS: the same name has been used for various other cells with an axon in at least three laminae, and the authors ask for it to be reserved for one
span.quote: The same name has been used for various other cells with axon in at least three laminae ( Hajos & Mody, 1997 ; Pawelzik et al. 2002 ), but we suggest retaining this name for this distinct type of cell.

span.label: AND THE SAME CELL UNDER SEVERAL NAMES: the O-LM cell was already described in 1893 under a Spanish descriptive name, and has been reported from other layers with identical axonal output under a different name again
span.quote: The horizontal dendrites in str. oriens and the axon mostly distributed in str. lacunosum-moleculare make them universally accepted and have given them their name ( McBain et al. 1994 ), but they were already described as ‘celula de cilindro-eje ascendente’ by Ramon y Cajal (1893) . They have been reported from other layers with identical axonal output under different name ( Oliva et al. 2000 ), but whether they received different input from those in str. oriens was not tested.

span.label: TWO CLASSES THAT MAY BE ONE THING CAUGHT AT TWO MOMENTS: the expression of the two distinguishing molecules may be dynamically regulated in time, making types 3 and 4 two STATES of one cell type
span.quote: As in further cases below, when so little information is available, it cannot be excluded that the expression of VIP and VGLUT3 is dynamically regulated in time and that types (3) and (4) are two states of one cell type. Further data on synaptic connectivity, additional molecular constituents known to occur in cortical CCK + interneurones such as CRF, preprotachikinin B, 5-HT3 receptor, etc., intrinsic membrane properties and in vivo firing patterns are needed to test this possibility.

span.label: and a controlled list that publishes its own uncertainty per entry - which classes may be lumped or split once enough is known, named individually
span.quote: Some of the above listed cell classes may be lumped or split further when sufficient information becomes available on all aspects that define a cell class with our criteria. In particular, the backprojection and septo-hippocampal cells (nos (12) and (13)), the two classes of perforant path-associated cells (nos (8) and (9)) and some of the three classes of interneurone specific cells (nos (14)–(16)) may prove to be members of a single population.

span.label: with the evidence weight behind each entry disclosed: some classes rest on one cell, or two, sometimes from one laboratory, and REVEALING HOW LITTLE WE KNOW MAY FACILITATE MORE DETAILED TESTS
span.quote: We would like to emphasize that on some cells very little information exists and sometimes even that only from one laboratory; but revealing how little we know may facilitate more detailed tests.

span.label: A PROPERTY OF THE TYPE IS STATE-DEPENDENT: during different oscillations representing two distinct brain states, cells of the same class show different firing patterns
span.quote: During different network oscillations representing two distinct brain states, interneurones of the same class show different firing patterns modulating their postsynaptic target-domain in a brain-state-dependent manner. These results suggest roles for specific interneurone types in structuring the activity of pyramidal cells via their respective target domains, and accurately timing and synchronizing pyramidal cell discharge, rather than providing generalized inhibition.

span.label: and the measurable local property does not predict the behaviour - in vivo firing is NOT simply determined by the main excitatory drive as predicted from where the dendrites sit, but by complex network phenomena
span.quote: Another fascinating question is how the different firing patterns of distinct interneurones are generated. The results so far indicate that the in vivo firing of a cell is not simply determined by its main excitatory drive as predicted from the laminar location of the dendrites, but is governed by complex network phenomena

span.label: with the sharpest case being a cell that falls silent exactly when its main excitatory input is most active, which weak excitation alone cannot explain
span.quote: The silence of O-LM cells during ripple episodes is surprising because they receive their major glutamatergic input from local CA1 pyramidal cells, which are most active as a population during ripples. The pyramidal input to O-LM cells has a very low resting release probability, which is increased only by repetitive firing ( Ali et al. 1999 ). Because pyramidal cells rarely fire more than one or two action potentials, this network state is not optimal for O-LM cell activation. However, the specific depression of firing of O-LM cells during ripple episodes cannot be explained by weak excitation alone. Additional mechanisms for silencing must be present in the network.

span.label: STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION ARE DECLARED INSEPARABLE: spatial and temporal measures reflect an indivisible unity of design, and neurones do not have separate structure or function
span.quote: Spatial and temporal measures of neurones in the network reflect an indivisible unity of evolutionary design, i.e. neurones do not have separate structure or function.

span.label: and even the population taken as uniform is not - the pyramidal cells generally considered a single population may be at least three groups that do not share inputs or response properties
span.quote: The pyramidal cells are generally considered to form a single population, but there may be at least three distinct groups, which do not necessarily share the same inputs and response properties.

span.quote: We have tested this hypothesis by recording the firing patterns of anatomically identified interneurones during network oscillations in anaesthetized rats ( Klausberger et al. 2003 , 2004 ).

span.label: contradicts → Hajos & Mody (1997) and Pawelzik et al. (2002), on the use of the name 'trilaminar cell'

span.quote: With the cited evidence we hope to convince our readers that some frequently used criteria about the identity of interneurones are unsustainable. (i) Somatic location in a layer does not identify an interneurone class, as the same class may have somata in several layers and all layers contain several distinct classes. (ii) Dendritic shape does not necessarily identify an interneurone class, as indistinguishable axonal output can be made by cells having diverse dendritic fields. (iii) A single molecular cell marker, such as a calcium binding protein or a neuropeptide, does not identify an interneurone class on its own, as most molecules have been shown to be expressed in several different cell types with distinct inputs and spatio-temporal outputs. span.quote: There is no agreement on the number and identity of neuronal species in the cerebral cortex. This is partly due to the lack of agreement on criteria of what is necessary to define a cell type, and consequently different authors use partial criteria or sets of non-overlapping data for studying the same or a mixture of several neuronal populations.

span.label: builds-on → the nineteenth-century hypothesis that neurones of different shape have distinct roles, and the neurotransmitter and output-location evidence that supported it
span.quote: The hypothesis that neurones with different shapes have distinct roles in the cortex was implicit in the earliest studies of Ramon y Cajal and was later elaborated by many, most elegantly by Janos Szentagothai (1975) . Key evidence for neuronal shape being indicative of role came from neurotransmitter identification, e.g. GABA via the immunocytochemical demonstration of glutamate decarboxylase (GAD) in smooth dendritic neurones and its absence from pyramidal cells ( Ribak, 1978 ). A further useful predictor for distinct roles was found in the differential and highly selective location of output synapses on target neurones ( Ramon y Cajal, 1893 ; Szentagothai, 1975 ; Somogyi et al. 1998 ). The use of biophysical measures, expression patterns of proteins involved in cell signalling, and, more recently, in vivo firing patterns have all proved useful in defining cell types

span.label: extends → connectivity-based classification, by adding in vivo firing phase as a fourth defining measure
span.quote: Here we attempt to define cell types first on the distribution of input and output synapses coupled with protein expression, then show that at least some cell types defined this way exhibit distinct firing patterns in vivo , placing each interneurone type to a distinct position in a multidimensional space of spatial, molecular and temporal measures.

span.label: generalises → the CA1 scheme to the isocortex, where most of the same types have homologues and the axo-axonic cell was first found
span.quote: Most of the GABAergic cell types defined in the CA1 area have homologues in the isocortex, which is particularly apparent in the supragranular layers. For example, the somata of supragranular pyramidal cells are innervated by basket cells immunopositive for PV, or CCK, or CCK and VGLUT3 ( Kawaguchi & Kubota, 1997 ; Somogyi et al. 2004 ) as in the hippocampus, and the axo-axonic cell was discovered in the rat visual cortex.

span.label: predicts → that the interneurone-specific type III cells fire strongly during ripples, since they are the independent GABAergic input to the cells that fall silent then
span.quote: From the major, and apparently independent, GABAergic input of O-LM cells from IS-III cells (see no. (16)), we predict that IS-III cells fire strongly during ripples. The consequences of the depressed firing of O-LM cells during ripple episodes remain unknown.
